rules.name: Stochastic process indexed-family definition
preconditions: A common probability space and index set are fixed
rules.operation: Interpret a stochastic process as a family of random variables indexed by time or another parameter.
examples: Discrete-time chains and continuous-time paths are both indexed random-variable families
counterexamples: A single isolated random variable is not by itself a process family

rules.name: Markov property seed
rules.output_form: future independent of past given present
preconditions: The process is evaluated in the active Markov model
rules.operation: Use the present state as a sufficient summary of the past for future evolution.
examples: Transition probabilities in a Markov chain depend only on the current state
counterexamples: Processes with memory of earlier states are not Markov in general

rules.name: Transition matrix power rule
rules.input_form: transition matrix P and step count k
preconditions: The chain is finite-state and time-homogeneous
rules.operation: Compose one-step transitions through matrix powers to obtain k-step transitions.
examples: Repeated one-step transitions compose through matrix powers
counterexamples: Using P^k for nonhomogeneous chains without adjustment is invalid

rules.name: Martingale conditional expectation rule
preconditions: Integrability and filtration-adapted hypotheses hold
rules.operation: Characterize martingale evolution through conditional expectation equality.
examples: Fair-game models satisfy the martingale recursion relative to their information filtration
counterexamples: Dropping integrability or filtration conditions is invalid

rules.name: Poisson process increment rule
preconditions: The process is the standard homogeneous Poisson process with rate lambda
rules.operation: Use independent stationary increment structure to identify interval count laws.
examples: Event counts over disjoint intervals are independent in a Poisson process
counterexamples: Nonstationary increment laws do not fit the standard homogeneous Poisson process

rules.name: Brownian motion covariance seed
preconditions: The process is standard Brownian motion
rules.operation: Use the covariance structure of standard Brownian motion.
examples: Covariance of Brownian values is governed by the overlap of the time intervals
counterexamples: Treating Brownian increments as deterministic is invalid

rules.name: Stationary distribution criterion
rules.input_form: distribution pi and transition matrix P
preconditions: The chain is finite-state and time-homogeneous
rules.operation: Check stationarity by one-step distribution invariance.
examples: Stationary distributions remain unchanged after one time step of the chain
counterexamples: Any distribution on the state space is not automatically stationary

rules.name: Detailed balance reversibility seed
rules.input_form: distribution pi and transition matrix P
preconditions: The chain is finite-state and the candidate stationary distribution is specified
rules.operation: Use detailed balance as a standard sufficient test for reversibility.
examples: Detailed balance gives a practical route to verifying reversibility and stationarity
counterexamples: Reversibility cannot be concluded from pi P = pi alone without the extra symmetry condition in general

rules.name: Optional stopping seed
preconditions: The stopping time and integrability hypotheses of the standard optional-stopping theorem hold
rules.operation: Preserve martingale expectation at suitable stopping times.
examples: Optional stopping transfers fairness from deterministic horizons to suitable random horizons
counterexamples: Applying optional stopping without checking its hypotheses is invalid

rules.name: Ito integral adaptedness seed
rules.input_form: Ito integrand relative to a filtration
preconditions: An Ito stochastic integral setting is active
rules.operation: Require integrands to use only present and past information in standard Ito integration.
examples: Stochastic integrals depend only on present and past information, not future paths, in the adapted Ito setting
counterexamples: Using future information inside a standard Ito integrand is invalid

rules.name: Stochastic differential equation Ito form seed
preconditions: An Ito diffusion model is specified
rules.operation: Decompose stochastic differential dynamics into drift and diffusion parts.
examples: Diffusion models split drift and noise through dt and dW_t terms
counterexamples: Treating dW_t as an ordinary differentiable increment is invalid

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions
